Halloween in Portugal: from Pão por Deus to Goat and Canhoto, how Portugal celebrates Witches' Day
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
09:22:55 UTC
18:22:55 KST

Carved pumpkins, sinister masks and children knocking on doors. Besides Halloween, "Pão por Deus" survives: in Portugal these are two ways to mark the year's scariest time.
Fake spider webs, witches' hats flying over ceilings, skeletons waving or glowing pumpkins smiling at us. This is the scene we now find in shops, schools and shopping centres. It means we are getting close to one of the scariest nights of the year: "Halloween".
Although it is not a tradition of Portuguese origin, it is no surprise that on the night of 31 October a group of children in scary costumes knock on our door for the traditional "doçura ou travessura" - "trick or treat" in the English version.
And although it is increasingly popular, Halloween is not the only event that marks this time of year. In Portugal there is another tradition which, despite the differences, has something in common with this imported celebration: children also go out into the streets and walk from door to door asking for offerings: it is "Pão por Deus".
This tradition is reserved for the morning of 1 November, All Saints' Day in Portugal - a public holiday when those who have passed away are remembered - and it is still kept alive in some places.
Although its origin is not agreed upon, it is believed that "Pão por Deus" emerged in the 15th century in a pagan context and is linked to ancient customs of sharing food in memory of the dead.
The tradition took on another dimension because of the 1755 earthquake, which struck Lisbon precisely on 1 November and left thousands of people in misery. According to this version, a year after the tragedy the poorest began the custom of going from door to door asking for bread to stave off hunger.
Nowadays it is mainly children who keep this practice alive, always with their cloth bags, often decorated by themselves or even handed out by local councils in some areas. The offerings also tend to be different: besides the traditional bread, cakes or dried fruit, people now give sweets or even money.
The tradition also involves reciting verses and songs, and there is no shortage of different quatrains: "Pão por Deus, Fiel de Deus, little cake in the bag, you walk with God"; or "Pão por Deus, for the love of God, put it here in the little bag, let everything be for the love of God". In some regions people also sang: "Little cakes and little cakes for me and for you, to give to the departed who are dead and buried".
The celebration takes different forms from region to region. In Estremadura it is known as "Dia do Bolinho", when the practice consists of giving traditional cakes of the season.
In the Azores one of the traditions linked to this time of year is caspiadas, cakes shaped like skulls in honour of the dead, which still survive in some places.
In Beira Baixa the tradition is more closely linked to godparents, who give a cake, the Santoro, to their godchildren.
The Portuguese tradition tends to be peaceful. Unlike what happens with the traditional "trick or treat", there is no such obvious link between refusing to give something and possible pranks. In Pão por Deus the spirit of sharing prevails, along with the desire to keep alive a tradition that is passed down from generation to generation.
Other traditional celebrations on "Halloween" night
There is a Portuguese celebration that comes close to the Celtic roots that gave rise to Halloween and is held in the north of the country, in a village in the district of Bragança, Cidões. It is called the "Festa da Cabra e do Canhoto" and is organised by the Associação Raízes Aldeia Cidões (source in Portuguese). (source in Portuguese)
As in the Celtic festival of "Samhain", which gave rise to Halloween, the tradition dictates that a large bonfire should be lit.
The "canhoto" that gives the festival its name is a large burning log and represents evil and hidden forces. The tradition also says that the canhoto and the firewood have to be stolen and will only burn if this condition is met.
Goat is cooked in large pots over the bonfire and roasted chestnuts are eaten.
It is around the bonfire that the ancestral tradition of Celtic origin is revived. The Celts, including the tribe of the Zoelas, lived in the Bragança and Vinhais region and at this time of year celebrated the farewell to the "bright season" to make way for the "dark season". It was believed that in this transition the world of the living and the world of the dead met.
The festivities are completed with Celtic-style performances such as dances, fire-breathers, pipers, drums and the arrival of the Careto, a figure from Trás-os-Montes, on an ox-drawn cart.
Further north, in the village of Vilar de Perdizes, in the municipality of Montalegre, the "Noite dos Fachos" is celebrated, a tradition full of mysticism. The participants, usually younger people, tend to "steal straw" and climb to the top of the mountains of the Serra do Larouco with the fachos (lit torches), shouting to scare away spirits, demons or witches.
The mountain range, at more than 1,500 metres above sea level, inherited the name of a Celtic deity, "Larouco", which helps to explain the link with these supernatural rituals.
Halloween, which only arrived in Portugal in the 1990s, was already well established in Vilar de Perdizes, which marks the Day of the Witches under the banner of the "Aldeia Assombrada" (source in Portuguese).
The true representation of globalisation
The Halloween tradition as we know it today is already a version shaped by many influences and customs. Its roots go back in part to the Celtic festival of "Samhain", held at the end of October and associated with the end of the harvests and the arrival of winter.
During this celebration it was believed that the world of the dead and the world of the living were closer together. The Celts thought that the spirits of the dead could return to the world of the living and, over time, customs emerged associated with this belief, such as lighting bonfires and wearing disguises.
From the 7th and 8th centuries onwards, with the spread of Christianity and the celebration of All Saints' Day on 1 November, pagan and Christian traditions began to influence each other, helping to shape the celebrations that we now associate with Halloween.
The term "Halloween" comes from the English expression "All Hallows' Eve", which means the eve of All Saints' Day.
However, it was also with Irish immigration to the United States between 1845 and 1849, during the devastating Great Famine in Ireland, that the tradition began to take new forms and to move closer to what we know today. In the United States costumes, illuminated pumpkins and other practices that we associate with this night became increasingly popular.
The city of Anoka in Minnesota calls itself the "Halloween Capital of the World" and is known for having organised in 1920 one of the first large-scale community celebrations dedicated to this date.
It was in this city that a parade was organised which helped to consolidate a tradition of public Halloween celebrations. Today its best-known symbols include pumpkins, witches, skeletons and other frightening costumes.
Other Halloween celebrations in Europe
In many European countries Halloween is celebrated in a way very similar to the North American tradition, but in some places there are very distinctive ways of marking the Night of the Witches. Here are some examples.
Transylvania, Romania
The region of Transylvania in Romania is now associated with the celebration of Halloween, largely thanks to the vampire imagery created by the Irish writer Bram Stoker in his 1897 novel "Dracula".
Bran Castle (source in Portuguese)is marketed as "Dracula's Castle" and has provided the perfect backdrop for Halloween celebrations, themed events and horror-inspired parties. Visitors are taken on a tour through a gloomy atmosphere, very much in the Halloween style.
Bruges, Belgium
From romantic streets to a dark setting, Bruges is transformed at Halloween.
From a storytelling session about the tale of the water ghost that is said to haunt the Lake of Love, to a night-time walk through the city's darkest legends, myths and stories, anything is possible on the night of 31 October.
The "Historium", an interactive and immersive tourist attraction located on the Markt (Market Square), also gets into the spirit with a spooky decoration of pumpkins, spider webs and bats, in the style of a haunted house. There is also a virtual reality experience dedicated to Halloween and a Museum of Torture for those brave enough.
Edinburgh, Scotland
In Edinburgh Halloween is taken very seriously with the Samhuinn Fire Festival (source in Portuguese), which is nothing more than a modern re-creation of the ancient Celtic traditions of the Scottish capital, with colourful costumes, fire performances and a lively procession through the cobbled streets.
This festival also exists in Sintra, Portugal, where it is held at Quinta da Ribafria.
Derry, Northern Ireland
In the city of Derry in Northern Ireland the roots of Halloween are also revived with the Derry Halloween festival.
Presented as one of the biggest Halloween festivals in Europe, the event features light shows, acrobatic banshees and circus performers inspired by Celtic traditions.
Visitors can also pick out pumpkins or take part in craft workshops before live music and performances take over after dark

- The Spanish train crash near Urda killed at least 69 people and left 64 missing. It is Spain’s deadliest rail accident since 2013.
- A preliminary report says the Renfe train was travelling at 160kmh to 200kmh. The crash followed signalling failure and control centre errors, with protocol ignored.
- The disaster has reopened safety concerns on Spain’s high-speed rail network. Investigators will use the black box to confirm the exact speed and cause.
AI generated
MADRID – The Spanish train that smashed into a second stationary one, killing at least 69 people on Oct 28, was travelling at a speed of at least 160kmh, according to a preliminary report about the accident.
The Civil Guard said it has received reports of 64 people missing in what is already Spain’s deadliest train accident since 2013.
The authorities have carried out 49 autopsies so far and identified five people, three women and two men, Esther Padilla, spokesperson for the Castilla-La Mancha regional government, said on state television network TVE.
“Testing is proceeding slowly, although families will be contacted throughout the day so that they can come and collect their results,” Padilla said on Oct 30.
It is unclear how many of the missing were among the bodies still to be identified.
The crash, which happened near the town of Urda in central Spain, followed another fatal accident in January involving the same rail companies on the same line. It has reopened a debate about safety and maintenance on Spain’s high-speed rail network, the most extensive in Europe.
The collision occurred after several trains were automatically stopped due to the failure of the automatic signalling system, after which the central control centre in Madrid took over.
A train operated by state-owned Renfe was authorised to proceed, even though there was a stationary Iryo-operated train ahead, according to Transport Minister Oscar Puente.
Audio of communications between the control centre and the train drivers obtained by El Pais showed how a controller authorised the Renfe train to continue on its journey at a normal speed, which Puente said disregarded a protocol to travel at no more than 40kmh in such circumstances.
The audio also showed the controller authorised the Renfe train, carrying 379 passengers and seven crew, to renew its journey when it should have been the Iryo train in front, which carried 147 passengers and five crew, to proceed first, according to protocol.
Sequence of malfunctions
“The sequence of malfunctions, instructions, and actions eventually led to the collision, in the absence of the necessary mitigating barriers,” according to the preliminary report by the Independent Authority for the Technical Investigation of Accidents and Incidents (AITAT).
It estimated that the Renfe train was travelling at a speed of between 160kmh and 200kmh when the collision occurred.
AITAT said it would not be able to confirm the exact speed of the train until it extracted information from the train’s black box.
“The scene was devastating. You saw carriages completely burnt out, as if they’d exploded. What you see coming out were people in a very bad way, and others who start pulling out the bodies of the deceased and placing them right there next to where we were,” Sebastian Herrero, who was travelling near the front of the Iryo train, said. Asylum applications drop 13% under EU migration pact
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
09:17:07 UTC
18:17:07 KST

Asylum applications drop 13% under EU migration pact
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
The number of first-time asylum applications in the Netherlands fell by 13% in the third quarter of 2026, compared with the same period last year, according to figures from national statistics bureau CBS and immigration service IND.
The downward trend follows the implementation of the new European Union Migration Pact, which came into effect in June this year, with tighter guidelines, the abolition of permanent asylum residence permits and stricter criteria for family reunification.
Several of those changes echo measures pushed by former asylum minister Marjolein Faber (PVV), who promised the “strictest asylum policy ever” and wanted to make the Netherlands “as unattractive as possible to asylum seekers”. Her emergency asylum law was rejected by the Senate in April.
In the third quarter of 2026, some 5,900 people filed an asylum application for the first time, 850 fewer than a year earlier. Asylum applications from Eritreans and Syrians halved, while 1,500 fewer family reunification applicants came to the country than a year ago.
Eritreans submitted the most asylum claims, followed closely by Syrians. According to CBS, the number of Ukrainian applications increased from 15 to 140, while the number of applications from people from Ethiopia decreased from 290 to 75.

Russia’s Defense Ministry proposes delaying December military pay until January
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
09:15:59 UTC
18:15:59 KST

Russia’s Defense Ministry has drafted an order that would postpone service members’ December pay to January for the first time in at least 18 years, the independent Russian news outlet Verstka reported.
Under current rules, service members are paid for the previous month between the 10th and 20th of each month, and for December, by December 25. The Defense Ministry wants to push the December payments back to January 11–21 of the following year.
If adopted, the changes could take effect as early as this year.
Service members of the Joint Group of Forces fighting in Ukraine would be exempt, continuing to be paid under the old schedule before the New Year. Contract soldiers would also be treated differently: in December, they are supposed to receive a bonus along with their pay.
Russian service members have received their December pay before the end of the calendar year since at least 2008, according to official records Verstka reviewed. The outlet said the practice was likely also observed during the Soviet era.
Authorities in Stavropol Krai decided to postpone until 2027 the payments to the families of those killed and wounded in the war, it was reported the day before. The payments are normally supposed to arrive within five business days of a claim’s approval, but authorities can delay payment if the regional Labor Ministry’s account lacks funds.
Regions have also been cutting payments to the families of the deceased one after another in recent months. In the Ulyanovsk region, the payments were cut by a factor of 20, while in the Saratov region, they were cut by a factor of 10.

Unknown Russian USV Attacks Container Ship That Sinks in Bulgarian Waters
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
09:15:53 UTC
18:15:53 KST

An unknown Russian naval drone was recorded attacking the CONTSHIP JET container ship in the Black Sea, which later sank off the Bulgarian coast.
Bulgarian outlet Maritime.bg published the video, while Reuters reported the preliminary identification of the vessel.
The footage, filmed from aboard the vessel, shows a USV approaching at high speed, moving alongside the container ship’s starboard side before turning towards its hull.
According to analysts at Ambrey Analytics, the vehicle is approximately 5–6 metres long and has a matte black hull. Its manoeuvring pattern may indicate that it is remotely controlled.
Experts believe the naval drone may be a modified version of the Russian Murena-300S vehicle or its derivative.
The Murena-300S is designed for reconnaissance, patrol and mine-laying missions. It can also be used as a kamikaze boat or an FPV drone carrier. Its stated operational range is up to 500 km.
The attack on the CONTSHIP JET took place on October 28 in Bulgaria’s exclusive economic zone, near Cape Kaliakra. The Liberian-flagged vessel was sailing from Haifa, Israel, to Constanța, Romania, when it was attacked by three naval drones.
The container ship sustained significant hull damage in the attack and sank off the Bulgarian coast. There were 18 crew members on board: 14 Filipino nationals and four Ukrainians. All crew members were rescued and taken to the port of Varna.
The vessel was carrying 421 containers, including those containing lithium-ion batteries, acids and industrial components.
According to Commander of the Bulgarian Navy, Kiril Mihaylov, the military received a warning about the threat of naval drones from a French patrol aircraft but was unable to prevent the attack.
In total, at least six civilian vessels were attacked by USVs off the Bulgarian coast in October.
Militarnyi previously reported on the specifications of Russian drones disclosed by the Defence Intelligence of Ukraine, including the Skanda reconnaissance USV, the Murena-300S and other strike platforms.

Fire Point is scaling up production of Flamingo missiles and FP-1 and FP-2 attack drones, Stielerman says
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
11:13:38 EET
18:13:38 KST

Fire Point is scaling up production of Flamingo missiles and FP-1 and FP-2 attack drones, Stielerman says
Kyiv • UNN
Fire Point is increasing production of FP-5 Flamingo missiles and FP-1 and FP-2 drones. The company is also developing FP-7 and FP-9 ballistic missiles.
Ukrainian weapons manufacturer Fire Point is scaling up production of the FP-5 Flamingo cruise missiles and FP-1 and FP-2 attack UAVs. In addition, the company is working on the production of the FP-7 and FP-9 ballistic missiles. This was reported by Fire Point co-founder and chief designer Denys Shtilerman, UNN writes.
Context
Earlier, a scandal erupted on social media over a wave of manipulations, prompted by a fragment of an old interview with Fire Point CEO Iryna Terekh that had been taken out of context and circulated in edited form. The video clip was edited in such a way as to suggest that Terekh had said the company had stopped producing FP-5 "Flamingo" cruise missiles. Fire Point CEO denied this information. In fact, the issue was not abandoning the "Flamingo," but rather the absence of plans to create additional cruise missile models.
Details
Denys Shtilerman emphasized that, on the contrary, the company is working to scale up production of the Flamingo, FP-1, and FP-2.
We continue to manufacture them (the "Flamingo" missiles — Ed.). Moreover, I guarantee that we are constantly scaling up production of both FP-5 cruise missiles and FP-1 and FP-2 drones, and are actively working on the production of FP-7 and FP-9 ballistic missiles
Shtilerman called the wave of manipulation about the cessation of missile production another attack on the company.
For me, it was hugely disappointing to see how some people eagerly spread a distorted statement from Iryna's interview without even checking the original source. In doing so, they help spread Russian narratives. The fact that the enemy is devoting so much effort to information warfare is yet another confirmation of our strength
Shtilerman noted that Ukraine is now stronger than ever in its history and is fighting against the entire "axis of evil."
Our army and our weapons are the best in the world. Direct proof of this is the incredible achievements on the battlefield and the fact that Ukraine initiated and is leading the project to create the pan-European "Freyja" ballistic shield. We need not to devour one another, but to unite in the fight against Russia, which is waging a genocidal war against Ukraine every day, and direct our forces toward victory. Let us all focus on this
To remind you
Freyja is a Ukrainian-initiated project for a joint European antiballistic system, the first track of the Antiballistic Coalition, which includes 10 countries and more than a dozen leading European defense companies. The system is intended to intercept Russian ballistic missiles.
The project is built around the Ukrainian FP-7.x interceptor missile developed by Fire Point, while the other components are supplied by European manufacturers. As reported by UNN, Fire Point Chief Executive and Technical Officer Iryna Terekh said that development had reached the stage of technical integration of the entire ecosystem — radars, a launcher, a data transmission channel, and a command center — while tests are conducted up to twice a week.
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported that Ukraine had completed its part of the work on the Freyja antiballistic project, while partner countries continue working on their part in order to proceed to testing the first system as soon as possible.

More than charity: the couple giving Israel's most vulnerable children a second chance
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
09:11:40 UTC
18:11:40 KST

Some partnerships begin with a donation and, over the years, become part of an organization's story. That has been the case for Jane and Larry Sherman and Orr Shalom, an Israeli organization that provides homes, stability and support for children, teenagers and young adults at risk, offering them the opportunity for a different future.
For more than 25 years, the Shermans have supported Orr Shalom out of a belief that every child deserves to grow up in a safe, loving and supportive environment. That commitment has guided their involvement with the organization through decades of philanthropy and changing needs.
While many charitable contributions focus on individual projects or limited periods, the Shermans' partnership has continued for more than two decades, growing alongside Orr Shalom and adapting to the needs of the children and young adults it serves.
A journey that began with a home
The couple's relationship with Orr Shalom began with the need to find a home for five Ethiopian children who had nowhere to go. The Shermans helped the organization establish a group home where the children could find stability, warmth and a sense of belonging.
Jane has described the connection as deeply personal, saying the couple came to regard the five children as members of their family. She credited their subsequent success to "the love and caring and stability they received" at the Orr Shalom group home where they grew up.
What began with those five children eventually expanded into support for Orr Shalom's Graduate Program, which helps young adults transition from out-of-home care to independent living.
For young people who grow up in residential care, turning 18 can bring significant challenges. Many leave the system without a stable support network or someone to help them navigate the practical demands of adulthood, from paying rent and pursuing an education to making their first independent financial and personal decisions.
Orr Shalom's Graduate Program was established to help bridge that gap. The Shermans' support for the initiative reflects their belief that responsibility for a child's well-being does not end on their 18th birthday.
A home named in their honor
Last week, Orr Shalom held a ceremony in Mevaseret Zion to honor Jane and Larry Sherman by renaming its family group home after them. The home, now known as Beit Sherman, recognizes their more than 25 years of involvement with the organization.
"Naming the family group home in Mevaseret Zion after Jane and Larry Sherman expresses our appreciation for more than 25 years of partnership," said Yair Medalion, CEO of Orr Shalom. "Jane has accompanied Orr Shalom's work from the founding of a home for children, through the development of the Graduate Program, and on to her support of foster care as a nurturing response. Their continued contribution affects the lives of many children and young people."
Beit Sherman continues to provide children with a warm, home-like environment. For those who grow up there in the coming years, the name will serve as a lasting reminder of the couple's commitment to helping children build more secure futures.
Changing needs in the wake of October 7
Ahead of the ceremony, Jane spoke with Naomi Segal on a Kan English podcast about her philanthropic work and the couple's longstanding involvement with Orr Shalom. The episode described her as a longtime leader in Jewish philanthropy whose connection to the organization, together with Larry, spans decades and remains deeply personal.
Their conversation also addressed the changing needs of Israeli society, particularly following the October 7 attacks and the ensuing war. Children and young adults already facing difficult circumstances have been especially vulnerable to the effects of the conflict, increasing the need for stable homes and reliable support systems.
Jane emphasized that children and young adults who were already considered at risk before October 7 have become even more vulnerable since the war began. Her comments highlighted the importance of adapting existing programs to meet new challenges while maintaining the support networks established over the years.
For a donor who has worked alongside an organization for decades, that continuity also provides an understanding of how children's needs evolve and why sustained support remains essential during periods of crisis.
The value of a long-term partnership
The story of Jane and Larry Sherman illustrates how philanthropy can extend beyond a single donation or project. A long-term partnership allows an organization to plan ahead, develop new programs and respond to changing circumstances, particularly during periods of crisis. It also reflects the trust that develops over time between donors and the organizations they support.
For Orr Shalom, the Shermans' involvement has helped establish a home for children, expand support for young adults leaving care and sustain the organization's work across generations.
Behind every home and every program are children and young people who need stability, care and someone willing to invest in their future. For more than 25 years, Jane and Larry Sherman have been part of that effort.

Philippines' Bangsamoro elects chief minister, ending over 7 years of interim rule
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
09:11:23 UTC
18:11:23 KST

Riyaz ul Khaliq
30 October 2026•Update: 30 October 2026
Lawmakers in the southern Philippines' Bangsamoro autonomous region elected Abdulraof "Sammy Gambar" A. Macacua as chief minister Friday, marking the transition from more than seven years of interim administration to an elected government, regional authorities said.
Macacua secured 51 votes against 27 for Murad Ebrahim during the first plenary session of the 80-member Bangsamoro Parliament in Cotabato City, the regional capital, according to an official statement.
One lawmaker was absent, while another abstained.
The assembly also elected lawyer Amer Zaakaria "Mikee" A. Rakim as speaker with 51 votes.
Both officials were sworn into office after the vote.
Earlier Friday, 79 of the 80 lawmakers took their oaths following the region's first parliamentary elections on Sept. 14.
The vote marked a milestone in a decades-long peace process that led to the establishment of the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) in 2019.
The region had been governed by an interim administration initially led by Ebrahim, chairman of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF).
Macacua, a former chief of staff of the Bangsamoro Islamic Armed Forces, succeeded Ebrahim in March 2025 after being appointed chief minister by Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
The elections followed the 2014 Comprehensive Agreement on the Bangsamoro, which paved the way for the creation of the Muslim-majority autonomous region and the transition from armed conflict to parliamentary governance.
The new parliament comprises 40 regional party representatives, 32 district representatives and eight sectoral representatives.
Macacua's Bangsamoro Federalist Party secured 16 seats in the elections, followed by Ebrahim's United Bangsamoro Justice Party (UBJP) with 15.

Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30

Petkov and Yotova in Bitola for the opening of a Bulgarian cultural club
				
				
			  
			
            Former Prime Minister and We Continue the Change (PP) leader Kiril Petkov plans to file a lawsuit against President Iliana Yotova over comments she made during a debate with Andrey Gyurov, the presidential candidate backed by the PP-DB coalition.
The dispute concerns the so-called Macedonian issue during Petkov’s government, particularly Bulgaria’s efforts to protect the rights of ethnic Bulgarians in North Macedonia through the French proposal.
Yotova accused Petkov of being ready to abandon Bulgaria’s position on Skopje at the last moment, saying the move was prevented only after an urgent consultative meeting called by then-President Rumen Radev.
“At the eleventh hour, Kiril Petkov was prepared to surrender the Bulgarian position regarding Skopje - a situation averted only thanks to an urgent consultative meeting convened by President Rumen Radev,” Yotova said.
Petkov rejected the accusation, saying the President had lied and effectively charged him with national treason. In a post on his official Facebook page, he argued that his government had secured a major diplomatic achievement by aligning Bulgaria’s position on North Macedonia with that of the entire European Union.
He accused Yotova of presenting what he described as an undeniable Bulgarian success as an act of betrayal.
Petkov also disputed her account of a joint trip to North Macedonia, saying it was neither intended for negotiations nor held in Skopje. According to him, the visit took place in Bitola for the opening of a Bulgarian cultural club.
“This photo with the balloons is from the only time Ms. Yotova accompanied me to North Macedonia. Was she 'defending the national interest' in front of the balloons at the new club? This is a lie that can be easily disproven,” Petkov wrote.
The former Prime Minister further challenged Yotova’s claim that his political camp had stopped Russian gas deliveries, forcing the subsequent agreement with Turkish state-owned company BOTAŞ.
Yotova had argued that Petkov and Asen Vasilev halted Russian gas supplies overnight, leaving the caretaker government with no choice but to seek an urgent alternative. She also said the BOTAŞ agreement would ultimately benefit Bulgaria.
Petkov countered that Gazprom had stopped deliveries because Bulgaria refused to comply with the Kremlin’s demand for payments in rubles, which he said would have breached the existing contract.
He also pointed out that the BOTAŞ agreement was signed by the caretaker government appointed by Radev, during whose presidency Yotova served as Vice President.
“It is one of the worst energy deals in Bulgaria’s modern history,” Petkov wrote.
Petkov said he had tasked a legal team with preparing a lawsuit against Yotova.
“See you in court, Ms. Yotova! Because your lies were ugly, malicious, and detrimental to Bulgaria’s interests,” he wrote at the end of his Facebook post.

Türkiye's economic confidence index falls 3.9% in October
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
09:09:37 UTC
18:09:37 KST

Gokhan Ergocun
30 October 2026•Update: 30 October 2026
Türkiye's economic confidence index fell 3.9% month-on-month to 97.3 in October, official data showed on Friday.
The drop pushed the index below the 100-point threshold, down from 101.3 in September, according to the Turkish Statistical Institute.
A reading above 100 indicates an optimistic economic outlook, while a reading below 100 reflects pessimism.
The decline was driven primarily by a sharp drop in consumer confidence, which sank 7.7% from the previous month to 84.8 in October.
Confidence in the real sector, representing the manufacturing industry, decreased 1.4% month-on-month to 101.1.
The services confidence index fell 2.4% from September to 109.2.
In contrast, the retail trade confidence index rose 1.1% on a monthly basis to reach 112.5.
The construction sector confidence index edged up 0.4% month-on-month to 83.3.

Türkiye's tourism revenue rises 5% to $25.5B in Q3
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
09:09:20 UTC
18:09:20 KST

Gokhan Ergocun
30 October 2026•Update: 30 October 2026
Türkiye's tourism revenue rose 5% year-on-year to $25.53 billion in the third quarter of 2026, official data showed on Friday.
Revenue generated directly from visitors amounted to $25.29 billion, while transit passenger income contributed $231.96 million, according to the Turkish Statistical Institute.
Turkish citizens residing abroad accounted for 14% of total tourism revenue during the July-September period.
Individual expenditures made up $17.11 billion of the quarterly total, while package tour spending stood at $8.18 billion.
The number of departing visitors slipped 1.6% year-on-year to 23.26 million in the third quarter.
Turkish citizens living abroad represented 13.6% of all visitors, totaling 3.16 million people.
Visitors staying overnight spent an average of $107 per night, while the average spending for expatriate Turkish citizens was $68 per night.
Package tours accounted for 32.3% of total expenditures, followed by food and beverages at 20.5% and accommodation at 12.5%.
Health-related expenditures jumped 23.6% compared to the third quarter of 2025, accommodation spending rose 19% and domestic transportation expenses climbed 12.1%.
Travel, entertainment, sports and cultural activities were the primary reasons for visiting Türkiye, cited by 74.5% of visitors, followed by visiting relatives and friends at 16.9% and shopping at 3.7%.
Among expatriate Turkish citizens, visiting relatives and friends was the leading motivation, accounting for 63.9% of visits.
Tourism expenditure, consisting of spending by Turkish residents traveling abroad, surged 22.6% year-on-year to $3.04 billion in the third quarter.
Individual spending abroad totaled $2.57 billion, while package tour expenses accounted for $467.64 million.
The number of Turkish residents traveling abroad increased 24.2% year-on-year to 4.2 million, with an average expenditure of $723 per person.

UK house prices grow at slowest pace in two years as mortgage rates rise
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
09:05:48 UTC
18:05:48 KST

UK house prices grew by an annual rate of just 0.5% in October, the slowest pace in more than two years, as higher mortgage rates put off potential buyers.
The average price for a property in the UK stood at £273,566 in October, flat on the previous month and down from 0.8% in the year to September, according to the lender Nationwide.
The slowdown in the market comes as buyers face higher borrowing costs. This month the average cost of a five-year fixed-rate mortgage hit the 6% barrier for the first time in three years.
The average stood at 5.99% on Thursday, according to the financial information provider Moneyfacts, while the average two-year rate was not far behind at 5.97%.
There has been no change in the Bank of England base rate since last December but volatility in the bond market has driven up the swap rates that influence the pricing of fixed-rate mortgages.
While the Bank of England has kept its key interest rate on hold at 3.75%, expectations are growing that next week the monetary policy committee will vote to increase the rate for the first time in three years to 4%.
Robert Gardner, the chief economist at Nationwide, said the Middle East conflict had fed concerns around inflation, driving up expectations of higher interest rates.
Property prices are likely to fall further, he said. “Surveyors report that new buyer inquiries remain weak.
“Consumer sentiment dipped noticeably in October, with households becoming less confident about the outlook for the general economy as well as their own financial situation in the year ahead.”
Tom Bill, the head of UK residential research at Knight Frank, added that the impact of rising mortgage costs “eclipses any support measure announced in this week’s budget”.
This week the chancellor, John Healey, confirmed the government’s new £4.7bn Your First Home scheme, which is designed to give a helping hand to first-time buyers who do not have access to the “bank of mum and dad”.
Bill added: “The absence of major shocks from the chancellor may produce a modest relief bounce in coming months. However, asking prices will need to reflect the much tougher financial landscape that buyers face.”
Rob Wood, the chief UK economist at the consultancy Pantheon Macroeconomics, said the government’s new scheme could provide a “modest boost” to the market but that prices were likely to remain subdued next year.

Russian independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta to close
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
09:05:21 UTC
18:05:21 KST

Novaya Gazeta, one of Russia’s best-known independent media outlets, has announced it will permanently close next month. The newspaper, whose former editor-in-chief Dmitry Muratov won the Nobel peace prize in 2021, cited intolerable pressure, including being stripped of its newsroom, its donation platforms and its legal right to publish.
“This is not just our own story; it is the story of a country and a society that are being systematically crushed,” wrote its editor-in-chief, Sergei Sokolov, on the newspaper’s website.
Launched in the 1990s and for many years partly funded by the late Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev, Novaya made its name through dogged, long-form reporting on corruption, rights abuses and social issues. Over the years, six of its journalists have been assassinated, including Anna Politkovskaya, who was gunned down in the stairwell of her Moscow apartment block in 2006.
While Novaya always swam against a tide of repression, the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 made independent reporting almost impossible and decimated the Russian media landscape. Novaya was one of the last critical voices still operating from inside the country.
“For nearly five years of ***, we managed to keep working while being completely encircled by the security services. Now it’s over. We have found ourselves in a ‘kill zone’,” wrote Sokolov. The stars were used in place of the word “war”, as under Russian law, journalists must refer to the war in Ukraine as a “special military operation” or face consequences.
The newspaper’s first response to the invasion was to put out a special bilingual Russian-Ukrainian edition in the days after Vladimir Putin launched the invasion. It described the war as “madness” on its front page. Soon after, the Kremlin implemented draconian new censorship laws, which forced media outlets to publish only the Russian official narrative about the conflict.
“We said it’s not journalism and we’re not going to do that,” said Nadezhda Prusenkova, the head of Novaya’s press service. The newspaper published blank white spaces instead of euphemisms and false information, to provide a visible reminder of the censorship laws.
By the end of March 2022, Novaya decided to stop publishing its print edition altogether, but the threats and pressure only increased. In April that year, Muratov was doused with red paint while on a train, an attack that damaged his eyesight and that US officials say was carried out on the orders of Russian intelligence agencies. In September that year, the newspaper’s official licence was taken away and soon after their website was blocked in Russia.
Novaya’s journalists, long used to operating in a hostile environment, found ways to circumvent the bans. Many left Russia, and a number of exiled former employees set up Novaya Gazeta Europe, a legally distinct outlet. Muratov and a core team stayed behind and continued to publish a series of magazines with a print run of 999 copies, taking advantage of a law that means magazines with under 1,000 copies do not require an official licence. Novaya’s website continued running, too, although the Russian state hit the outlet with various new legal threats.
“The fact Novaya kept working for this four and a half years after everything that happened was a miracle, but it was not just a miracle, it was also the daily choice of people who continued to go to work even when it was very scary,” said Elena Kostyuchenko, a former Novaya journalist who spent 17 years at the newspaper. “Today I feel very inspired by my colleagues, but also very painful and sad for them, and for all of us.”
In recent months, Prusenkova said the pressure had become intolerable. In April, the journalist Oleg Roldugin was arrested and charged with “unlawful access to computerised information”. He is under house arrest awaiting trial and last month Sokolov’s home was searched as part of the case.
This month, the newspaper’s landlords informed Novaya staff that they must vacate their longstanding office premises in central Moscow by 9 November. The newsroom has been the hub of the newspaper for decades and houses a memorial museum to Politkovskaya in the former office of the murdered journalist. Prusenkova said the exhibits would be taken down and put into storage, for now.
On top of the eviction notice, all the outlet’s donation platforms have been shut down, leaving the paper without any source of funding. The court case, combined with the eviction and the lack of funds, gave the newspaper no choice but to close, said staff.
“Sometimes it happens that your enemies win. At this moment in time, it seems like they have won, and we have no options left,” said Prusenkova. But she said it was probable Novaya’s journalists would try to find some way to continue their work. “After all, we don’t know how to do anything else,” she said.

Russian-Made Murena Drone Sank CONTSHIP JET Off Bulgaria's Black Sea Coast?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
09:05:00 UTC
18:05:00 KST

Russian-Made Murena Drone Sank CONTSHIP JET Off Bulgaria's Black Sea Coast?
The maritime drone that struck the Greek container ship CONTSHIP JET off Cape Kaliakra was likely a Russian-developed Murena-300S or a modified version of that model, according to security experts, while its exact origin and responsibility for the attack remain unconfirmed.
Stayko Topalov, president of the International Anti-Drone Association, said on Nova TV that his assessment was based on the available footage and consultations with other specialists. He said experts were 99% certain that the drones were Russian, describing them as older units that had undergone substantial modifications using advanced Russian technology.
Topalov said the device appeared to be a newer version of the Murena-300S rather than the older model available online. Its construction showed considerable precision, its hydrodynamics had been improved, and it was probably controlled remotely through a satellite connection, possibly using a joystick.
“There has been talk of the 'Murena-300S' - the older version, which can be found online, but what we see here is a new variant. It is clearly manufactured with great precision. The drone is most likely controlled via satellite link. Its hydrodynamics have also been improved. At present, it is likely operated using a joystick,” Topalov said.
He also drew attention to the way the drone approached the vessel, saying the footage suggested that the operator wanted the crew to see it before impact.
“We can see from the footage that the drone is approaching. Most likely, the operator wants to warn the people - after all, they know that these devices are used to kill. Furthermore, it is clear that the drone makes an approach, executes a maneuver, and then crashes into the ship. This is quite interesting - it seems there is an intentional effort to be noticed early on,” Topalov said.
The expert said such unmanned vessels could be countered by disrupting their GPS signals or using other methods, including kinetic measures. He argued that the most effective response would be to detect them at a distance and destroy them before they could reach their targets.
According to Topalov, the drones travel at speeds of 50 to 70 kilometers per hour and can carry between 200 and 300 kilograms of explosives.
He also questioned whether the circulating footage was authentic, although he said the level of detail visible on the ship's deck could indicate that it was genuine.
“Even children can create videos like this nowadays. That said, the footage shows a significant amount of detail from the ship's deck; this suggests the video might be genuine, though it could also have been manipulated,” said Topalov, who also heads the International Association for Countering Drones.
He warned that Bulgaria might not have the capacity to prevent an attack of this kind and urged politicians to stop offering what he described as false reassurance.
“I don't think we have the capability to prevent such an incident. Politicians should stop trying to reassure people and giving them false assurances and false hopes. It would result in a truly horrific incident. If there are 200 kilograms of explosives, half the port would vanish,” Topalov said.
Vesela Cherneva, deputy director of the European Council on Foreign Relations, and journalist Hristo Rimpopov also discussed the drone attacks on Black Sea shipping on NOVA NEWS.
Cherneva said establishing who was responsible would matter most if it helped countries prepare a coordinated response to future incidents with their NATO allies.
“Identifying the perpetrator is meaningful when a state is attempting to prepare for a future occurrence of this kind - in other words, the point is to say: 'This drone originates from Russia; therefore, we intend to take the following actions together with our NATO allies.' That is when the conversation with all the allies in the Alliance takes place,” Cherneva said.
She also criticized attempts to shift responsibility for attacks in Romanian waters onto Romania, stressing that Bulgaria and its neighbor were allies facing the same security risks. Cherneva said Romania had taken considerably more steps to strengthen its defenses, including hosting multinational forces and inviting aircraft from NATO member states to protect its airspace.
“At this particular moment, shifting the blame for Russian attacks onto Romania is, frankly, not very wise. They are our allies and our closest neighbor - we share the same fate. Unlike us, Romania has done significantly more to strengthen its own security. They host multinational forces, and there are aircraft from NATO member states guarding Romanian airspace - at Romania's own invitation,” she said.
Cherneva added that Romania currently felt more secure than Bulgaria.
Rimpopov said Bulgaria had spent years failing to develop its own defense capabilities and expressed hope that the recent provocations would lead to improvements in its role as a NATO ally.
“For years, Bulgaria has been slow to develop its own capabilities; now, I hope that something positive will emerge from these provocations and that we will become a reliable NATO ally,” Rimpopov said.
He argued that Russia was trying to exploit weaknesses in Bulgaria's defenses and that identifying the aggressor should take precedence over calls for peace without conditions.
“What we need to do is actually identify the aggressor, rather than just talking about peace at any cost. There must be peace, but it needs to be achieved in a way that ensures it is sustained in the long term,” the journalist said.
An assessment by international maritime security and risk management company Ambrey, reported by Reuters, also identified the unmanned vessel as likely belonging to the Russian Murena-300S family or being based on that design. Reuters verified the authenticity of video footage showing one of the drones shortly before it hit the ship.
Tomas Alexa, a senior analyst at Ambrey Analytics, said the craft displayed features consistent with Russian development.
“Ambrey assesses that the unmanned surface vessel is likely a variant of the Russian 'Murena-300S' model or was developed based on it,” Alexa told Reuters.
The footage, believed to have been recorded by a crew member, shows a matte-black unmanned craft measuring approximately 5 to 6 meters approaching the container ship at high speed. It initially moves parallel to the vessel before turning sharply toward its hull. A separate recording captures the explosion, after which the ship begins to list.
Aleksa said the drone's maneuvers indicated that it was being controlled remotely rather than operating autonomously. Former Ukrainian naval officer Andriy Ruzhenko also told Reuters that the craft did not resemble any known naval drone models used by Ukraine's armed forces.
The Murena-300S was developed by the Center for Unmanned Systems design bureau in the Russian city of Tula, according to information published by Dnevnik. The model was unveiled in 2024 and is intended for a range of potential missions, including reconnaissance, patrols, attacks on maritime and coastal targets, counter-mine operations, and the deployment of naval mines.
The craft can operate as a kamikaze vessel carrying explosives or serve as a launch platform for smaller FPV drones. Published specifications give it an operational range of at least 500 kilometers and a cruising speed of around 45 kilometers per hour, or more than 24 knots. Its payload capacity is at least 500 kilograms, with the ability to carry between 25 and 300 kilograms of explosives depending on its configuration. The hull is approximately 5.7 meters long.
Dnevnik also pointed to footage from the Murena-300S trials showing an antenna for the American satellite system Starlink. The Russian developer has presented the vessel as suitable for combating enemy naval drones and attacking ships, bridges, and coastal infrastructure.
Posts by the design bureau's representatives on the specialized Russian blog Takticheskiy ("Tactical") explicitly identify the Black Sea as a potential primary deployment area for the Murena.
A similar unmanned vessel was reportedly discovered near Romania more than two months ago. According to Dnevnik, the naval warfare website Covert Shores then published information about an unidentified drone found near the Romanian gas platform Neptun Alpha. The craft reportedly resembled the one seen in the footage from the attack off Cape Kaliakra. Before it was discovered, a Romanian F-16 fighter jet had fired on it, and it was identified as Russian.
However, the resemblance alone does not establish that the drone used against the CONTSHIP JET was Russian.
The exact perpetrators of the attack have not been identified, Reuters reported. The CONTSHIP JET, a Liberian-flagged container ship operated by a Greek company, was hit by three maritime drones on October 28 within Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone but outside its territorial waters.
The vessel was carrying 421 containers from the Israeli port of Haifa to Constanța, Romania, when it sustained severe damage and sank. All 18 crew members, comprising 14 Filipinos and four Ukrainians, were rescued and taken to Varna.
The drone visible in the footage has an elongated, wedge-shaped hull, a straight bow, and flat deck hatches intended for cargo or internal modules, writes security analyst Ruslan Trad from Capital media. A powerful outboard motor is visible at the stern, while a large mast at the rear carries a navigation radar and an electro-optical targeting system.
According to Trad, the craft does not correspond exactly to any widely documented serial model in publicly available sources, suggesting it could be an experimental prototype or a limited-production military development.
"Its tall mast is designed to raise communications and radar equipment above the waves, extending its range and maintaining a clear line of sight. This differs from Ukrainian platforms such as the Magura V5, which use satellite connectivity through Starlink and flat-panel antennas and maintain a low profile, rising only about 50 centimeters above the water," said the security analyst.
Trad further writes that "Ukrainian manufacturers use internal water-jet propulsion and specific Western electronic components, while the drone found near Kaliakra has a conventional outboard motor and engineering features associated with the Russian military-industrial complex. This design may have been chosen to compensate for the absence of Western satellite infrastructure."
"The differences in propulsion, overall shape and control method contradict claims circulating on social media that the vessel was a Ukrainian Magura."

Russian attacks across Ukraine kill 27, injure 128 over past day as 'horrific attack' strikes Dnipro train station

Russian attacks across Ukraine kill 27, injure 127 over past day as 'horrific attack' strikes Dnipro train station
At least 27 people were killed and 127 injured in Russian attacks across Ukraine over the past day, with a daytime drone strike on Dnipro's train station accounting for the highest number of casualties, local authorities said.
A Russian attack struck a platform at Dnipro railway station on the morning of Oct. 29, killing at least 15 people and injuring at least 14 others, regional governor Oleksandr Hanzha said.
A passenger train was preparing to depart for Zaporizhzhia when the station was struck by a Russian jet-powered drone, Ukrainian Railways wrote on social media. According to Ukraine's Air Force, Dnipro was targeted by four Russian jet-powered drones at around 11 a.m., three of which were shot down by Ukrainian air defenses before reaching their targets.
"A horrific Russian attack on Dnipro train station," President Volodymyr Zelensky wrote on social media in response to the attack. "The Russians used a drone to attack a platform where a regular commuter train and a regular passenger train were standing."
International leaders reacted throughout the day, condemning the attacks against the backdrop of reported progress in peace negotiations.
Later in the day, Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov reported that a Russian drone struck the dormitory of a vocational school in Dnipro, setting the entire fifth floor on fire. There were no injuries, Filatov said, as the students had managed to reach the shelter before the strike.
Throughout the day, Russian attacks across Dnipropetrovsk Oblast injured four more people, including a 15-year-old girl, Hanzha said in an evening statement on Oct.29.
Following the Russian attacks overnight, about 350,000 people in the oblast were left without electricity, Hanzha said in the early morning.
Beyond strikes on Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Russia launched ballistic missiles, four guided aerial missiles, and 113 Shahed-type drones, including 83 jet-powered drones, against Ukraine overnight on Oct. 30, according to Ukraine's Air Force.
The main targets of the attack were in Kyiv, Poltava, and Dnipropetrovsk oblasts, according to the Air Force.
Ukrainian air defenses intercepted or suppressed three of the guided missiles and 96 Russian Shahed-type drones, including 71 jet-powered drones, across 17 locations, the Air Force said.
The Air Force did not specify how many Russian ballistic missiles were launched or how many were intercepted.
In Chernihiv Oblast, Russian forces struck central Chernihiv in northern Ukraine around noon on Oct. 29 with Banderol cruise missiles, killing two 15-year-old girls, regional governor Viacheslav Chaus said.
The attack injured 25 other people, including four children, Chaus said. The youngest child is 10 months old, while the others include a 10-year-old girl and boys aged 16 and 17, he added. Eight people remain hospitalized.
Oct. 30 has been declared a day of mourning in Chernihiv.
In the city of Kremenchuk in Poltava Oblast, at least three people were killed and 32 injured, including six children, after Russian drones struck an apartment building in a residential area, regional governor Vitalii Diakivnych said.
Oct. 30 has been declared a day of mourning in Poltava Oblast.
In Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Russian attacks killed two people and injured 23 others, including a child, over the past day, the local authorities said.
In eastern Donetsk Oblast, Russian attacks over the past day injured five people, regional governor Vadym Filashkin said.
Russian attacks over the past day killed four people and injured 21 others in Kharkiv Oblast, regional governor Oleh Syniehubov said.
Four people were killed and 12 others injured in a Russian attack on the city of Izium, while six people were injured in Lozova. Three more people were injured in separate attacks in the city of Kharkiv, the village of Shevchenkove, and the village of Zatyshshia.
Russian forces attacked the oblast using FPV drones, other types of drones, glide bombs, and missiles, Syniehubov added.
In southern Kherson Oblast, a localized ceasefire aimed at allowing the evacuation of people from Russian-occupied Oleshky remains in effect. Regional governor Oleksandr Prokudin reported that one person was injured by the explosion of a Russian mine. No shelling or strikes targeting civilian or critical infrastructure were recorded over the past day, he said.
In Kyiv, Russian ballistic missile and drone attacks overnight killed one person and injured another, according to the Kyiv City Military Administration. In the Dniprovskyi District, a residential building was damaged in the attack, while a fire broke out at a non-residential building in the Darnytskyi District.
In Sumy Oblast, Russian attacks over the past day injured one person, according to the regional military administration. Russian forces attacked nine communities in the oblast using artillery, mortars, FPV drones, other drones, and glide bombs.

Hsiao calls for trusted drone supply chain at Taiwan forum
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
09:02:49 UTC
18:02:49 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim (蕭美琴) called for a China-free drone supply chain and closer international cooperation at the 2026 Taiwan Drone Forum on Friday, CNA reported.
Hsiao said that although Taiwan entered the drone industry relatively recently, it has strengths in semiconductors, precision engineering, and advanced manufacturing. She added that Taiwan’s drone exports in the first half of 2026 exceeded those for all of 2025.
Hsiao said President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) aims to strengthen Taiwan’s self-defense and deterrence through drone development. The government’s approach combines security needs with civilian innovation and international cooperation, she said.
Hsiao also praised the Global UAV Academy for connecting the public and private sectors and promoting international cooperation. She outlined three priorities for strengthening Taiwan’s position in the drone supply chain for democracies: trusted components, AI and software innovation, and international partnerships.
On supply chains, Hsiao said authoritarian regimes exploit backdoors and other countries’ dependence on their products. She said democracies need reliable alternatives and that Taiwan aims to ensure components such as microprocessors and flight controllers meet cybersecurity and operational standards.
On technology, Hsiao said AI and software innovation are crucial to drone development. Taiwan is integrating AI into autonomous platforms to enable real-time decisions and navigation when GPS is unavailable, she said.
On international cooperation, Hsiao said Taiwan should work with other countries on research and development, technology transfer, production, and procurement. She said its development and mass-production capabilities could help meet global demand.
Hsiao cited the foreign ministry’s donation of four maritime patrol and rescue drones to Palau, along with training, as an example of drone diplomacy, per CNA. Taiwan can also strengthen cooperation by sharing its expertise in civilian applications, she said.

Xi holds talks with German president

21.47% of students earn top grade in Taiwan English listening test
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
09:02:28 UTC
18:02:28 KST

TAIPEI (Taiwan News) — A total of 21.47% of students who took Taiwan’s first Test of English Listening Comprehension (TELC) for the 2027 academic year earned the top grade, down from 22.59% in the same session last year, according to statistics released Friday by the College Entrance Examination Center.
A total of 90,914 students registered for the test, which was administered across 33 examination districts and 2,647 testing rooms. The overall absentee rate was 3.6%, up 0.26 percentage points from 3.34% in the first test session last academic year.
TELC grades are divided into four levels: A (almost full comprehension), B (general comprehension), C (partial comprehension), and F (minimal comprehension). Of the 87,644 students who sat for the exam, 21.47% earned an A, 37.15% a B, 36.12% a C, and 5.26% an F.
The test consists of 40 items across five sections: picture description, question-response, conversations, short talks, and long-passage listening.
Students performed best in the conversations section, with a correct-answer rate of 73.29%, followed by picture description at 67.37% and question-response at 65.17%. Short talks and long-passage listening had the lowest correct-answer rates, at 61.16% and 60.57%, respectively.
Among students earning an A, correct-answer rates exceeded 90% in four of the five sections, with conversations producing the highest rate at 96.88%. Their correct-answer rate for long-passage listening was slightly lower, at 89.77%.
For students earning a B, correct-answer rates ranged from 69.26% for long-passage listening to 85.16% for conversations. Students earning a C performed best in conversations, at 54.26%, while those receiving an F had their lowest correct-answer rate in long-passage listening, at 19.85%.
Compared with the average results of the first test sessions over the previous four academic years, this year’s distribution showed a slightly higher proportion of C grades, at 36.12%, up 1.13 percentage points. The proportions of A, B, and F grades were slightly lower, by 0.21, 0.6, and 0.32 percentage points, respectively.
Overall, the results showed little difference between male and female students. Boys accounted for 48.36% of test takers and girls 51.64%. Boys had higher proportions of both A and F grades, while girls had higher proportions of B and C grades.
The center reported 350 examination violations, down 99 from 449 during the same testing session last academic year. The most common violation involved students failing to present an original, valid identification document, accounting for 321 cases, compared with 412 a year earlier.

Five Chinese golfers advance at Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
17:02:28 CST
18:02:28 KST

AUCKLAND, New Zealand, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Defending champion Fifa Laopakdee of Thailand maintained his lead after the second round of the 2026 Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship at Te Arai Links in New Zealand on Friday, carding a one-over 72 to reach seven under par for a 36-hole total of 135, two strokes clear of the field.
Five of the seven Chinese golfers competing in the tournament made the cut, with Wu Qiyou leading the Chinese contingent in a tie for sixth.
The 72-hole stroke-play tournament features a cut after 36 holes, with the top 60 players and ties advancing to the final two rounds. After Friday's second round, the cut fell at 155, or 13 over par, with 62 players qualifying for the next round.
Laopakdee, who secured Thailand's first AAC title last year, started his second round from the 10th tee on Friday morning. He was two under par through his first nine holes, but faced tougher conditions as the wind picked up after the turn. He eventually signed for a one-over-par 72.
"As you can see it's a little windy," said Laopakdee, 21. "Overall, it was a grind out there for me. Had a great front nine, shot two under par, then back nine, just didn't make any putts. Got two 3-putts and then coming down the stretch had a great chance of birdies but I just missed all of them. But if you ask me all week, I would take seven under for the first two rounds, and I think I'm in good position for the weekend."
Wu sits in a tie for sixth after two rounds, six strokes behind Laopakdee. He carded six birdies and seven bogeys on Friday to finish one over par for the round.
"There's been a lot of mistakes, and that's something I can work on over the next two rounds. In these windy conditions, the wind has a big impact on the putting line. It's important to get used to the tougher conditions and try to avoid taking more than two putts on each green," Wu said.
Chinese golfers Li Zhi, Zhou Ziqin, Hou Zenghao and Wang Yixiang also made the cut, while Cui Jingguo and Liu Yiming missed out on the final two rounds.
The 17th edition of the championship runs from October 29 to November 1 on Te Arai Links' South Course, with 120 players from 39 countries and regions competing in the 72-hole stroke-play event.
The winner will earn invitations to the 2027 Masters Tournament, the 155th Open Championship and the 132nd Amateur Championship. ■

COLOMBO, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- Sri Lankan investigators have begun extracting data from the Department of Motor Traffic's (DMT) computer systems as part of an investigation into alleged fraud and corruption, local media reported Friday.
The operation involves officers from the Walana Anti-Corruption Unit, supported by technical specialists from the University of Colombo School of Computing, Sri Lanka Computer Emergency Readiness Team (CERT), GovTech Sri Lanka and Sri Lanka Telecom.
Investigators are examining the department's digital records to identify possible irregularities and suspected fraudulent activities reported to have occurred over an extended period.
The investigation comes amid longstanding concerns over corruption at the department.
In June, Transport Minister Bimal Rathnayake told Parliament that findings by the Committee on Public Accounts and the Auditor General's Department concerning alleged corruption at the DMT would be referred to the Attorney General's Department and the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption.
Earlier, in March, four current and former DMT officials were remanded over allegations including fraudulent vehicle registrations and the manipulation of computerized records.
Authorities have not publicly disclosed the findings of the latest data examination or identified any suspects in connection with the operation. ■

Yemen has been mired in conflict since late 2014, when the Houthis seized Sanaa and much of northern Yemen, prompting the Saudi-led coalition to intervene in 2015 in support of the Yemeni government. ■

France's GDP contracts 0.1 pct in Q3
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
17:02:14 CST
18:02:14 KST

PARIS, Oct. 30 (Xinhua) -- France's gross domestic product (GDP) contracted 0.1 percent in the third quarter of 2026, according to preliminary data released Friday.
The decline came despite continued growth in final domestic demand excluding inventories. Household consumption accelerated, rising by 0.4 percent after a 0.2-percent increase in the second quarter, while government consumption grew by 0.3 percent, following a 0.4-percent increase.
Overall, final domestic demand excluding inventories contributed 0.1 percentage points to GDP growth, unchanged from the previous quarter, according to figures published by the French National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE).
The contribution of foreign trade to GDP growth turned negative in the third quarter, subtracting 0.6 percentage points from growth, compared with a positive contribution of 0.6 percentage points in the previous quarter. Exports fell by 1.7 percent, reversing a 2.8-percent increase in the second quarter, while imports remained almost unchanged, rising by 0.1 percent after a 0.9-percent increase.
INSEE added that France's consumer price index is expected to surge by 3.4 percent year on year in October, up from 3.1 percent in September.
Inflation is expected to accelerate mainly due to energy prices, which are set to rise for the fourth consecutive month, particularly because of higher gas and petroleum product prices.
"Growth has been absent for three consecutive quarters," the country's Economy and Finance Minister Roland Lescure said Friday in an interview with local broadcaster Franceinfo. "If we do not achieve the fiscal consolidation set out in the budget, we will hit a wall." ■

Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan sign 14 cooperation documents at interregional forum
Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan have signed 14 documents on interregional, interagency and business cooperation during the II Kazakhstan-Kyrgyzstan Interregional Cooperation Forum in Bishkek, Qazinform News Agency reports.
The forum, titled “The Role of Regions in Developing Strategic Partnership,” is co-chaired by Kazakh Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov and Chairman of the Kyrgyz Cabinet of Ministers and Head of the Presidential Administration Adylbek Kasymaliev.
The following documents were signed in the field of interregional cooperation:
- A Memorandum of Cooperation between the administration of East Kazakhstan region and the Office of the Presidential Plenipotentiary Representative in Kyrgyzstan’s Issyk-Kul region.
- An Agreement on establishing twin-city relations and developing cooperation between the Shchuchinsk-Burabay resort area in Kazakhstan’s Akmola region and the Issyk-Kul Lake resort area in Kyrgyzstan’s Issyk-Kul region.
- A Memorandum of Understanding between Almaty region and the Office of the Presidential Plenipotentiary Representative in Kyrgyzstan’s Jalal-Abad region.
- A Memorandum of Understanding between Kyzylorda region and the Office of the Presidential Plenipotentiary Representative in Kyrgyzstan’s Jalal-Abad region.
- A Memorandum of Understanding between Karaganda region and the Office of the Presidential Plenipotentiary Representative in Kyrgyzstan’s Jalal-Abad region.
- A Memorandum of Cooperation between the adinistration of Zhetysu region and the Office of the Presidential Plenipotentiary Representative in Kyrgyzstan’s Naryn region.
- An action plan for 2026–2030 to implement the Agreement on establishing twin-city relations between the administration of Almaty and Bishkek Mayor’s Office, signed on December 12, 1997.
- A Memorandum on establishing twin-city relations between Turkistan and the city of Manas in Kyrgyzstan’s Jalal-Abad region.
In the healthcare sector, the following agreement was signed:
- An Agreement between the ministries of healthcare of Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan on cooperation in cross-country procurement of medicines and medical devices.
The following documents were signed in the field of business cooperation:
- A contract between Kazakhstan’s Dobrye Traditsii and Kyrgyzstan’s Prod Impex LLC for the supply of canned products.
- A distribution agreement between Kazakhstan’s Dobrye Traditsii LLP and Kyrgyzstan’s Alaiku Organics LLC for the supply of traditional beverages.
- A distribution agreement between Kazakhstan’s Satu Company LLP and Kyrgyzstan’s Alaiku Organics LLC for the supply of traditional beverages.
- A cooperation agreement between Kazakhstan’s Astana Motors and Kyrgyzstan’s Trust Technologies LLC (IVOX Group) to promote Kazakh-made commercial and special-purpose vehicles on the Kyrgyz market.
- A Memorandum of Cooperation between Kazakhstan’s GT OilService and Kyrgyzstan’s Tan Auto LLC to promote FerTurino motor oil on the Kyrgyz market.
Earlier, it was reported that Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov arrived in Bishkek on an official visit.
The II Kazakhstan-Kyrgyzstan Interregional Cooperation Forum has kicked off at the Ala-Archa State Residence in Bishkek today.
Addressing the forum, Bektenov said that Kazakhstan’s trade turnover with Kyrgyzstan reached $2.3 billion in 2025, up 33% year-on-year.

Beijing said on Friday that claims that Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot were "groundless speculation".
"The report in question is based on groundless speculation and is nothing more than an attempt to smear China," foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a regular briefing, referring to an article in The New York Times.
The report said that US intelligence officials concluded that a Chinese executive linked to Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed acted as a Chinese intelligence asset funnelling information to Beijing.
The firm was under scrutiny for possibly steering advanced Nvidia AI chips to China, the report said, citing unnamed sources briefed on the investigation.
But the executive Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le and no relation to Jensen Huang, developed a close relationship with the Nvidia boss, the New York Times said.
Nvidia said that Megaspeed was like any other regional customer and that it had previously investigated and debunked claims the Singaporean company was smuggling chips to China, the report added.
"Jensen's interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a C.E.O.'s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year," Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo told the newspaper.

Philippines raises Mayon volcano alert following explosive eruption
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
09:02:07 UTC
18:02:07 KST

Philippines raises Mayon volcano alert following explosive eruption
The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) confirmed the alert upgrade, warning of increased volcanic activity and the potential for further eruptions.
According to PHIVOLCS, the eruption produced a dense ash plume that rapidly rose approximately 3,000 meters above the volcano's summit crater. Moderate winds carried the plume west-southwest, with ashfall expected in the communities of Daraga, Guinobatan and neighboring municipalities in Albay province.
The agency explained that Alert Level 3 indicates a significant increase in volcanic activity, including sustained volcanic earthquakes and powerful emissions of steam and ash.
PHIVOLCS warned that Mayon has entered a new phase of magmatic eruption, increasing the likelihood of lava flows in the coming days and weeks.
Authorities also cautioned residents about potential volcanic hazards, including lava flows, rockfalls and other dangerous phenomena associated with increased volcanic activity.
Mayon volcano, also known as Mount Mayon, is an active stratovolcano located in Albay province in the Bicol region of the Philippines, on the southeastern part of Luzon Island. It is among the country's most closely monitored active volcanoes due to its history of eruptions and potential risks to nearby communities.

WHO names candidates for director-general
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-30
09:02:01 UTC
18:02:01 KST

WHO names candidates for director-general
Seven candidates will compete to become the World Health Organization’s next director-general. Member states submitted their nominations ahead of the May 2027 election, Qazinform News Agency reports.
WHO announced the candidates on October 29. Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Belgium, Spain, Indonesia, China and Botswana each proposed a nominee.
Hanan Mohammed Al-Kuwari, nominated by Qatar, served as public health minister from 2016 to 2024. She also led Hamad Medical Corporation from 2007 to 2024. She now advises Qatar’s prime minister on public health affairs. Al-Kuwari chaired WHO’s Executive Board in 2023-2024.
Hanan Balkhy, Saudi Arabia’s nominee, became WHO’s regional director for the Eastern Mediterranean in February 2024. Previously, she served as WHO’s assistant director-general for antimicrobial resistance from 2019 to 2024. A physician specializing in pediatric infectious diseases, she also led infection prevention programs in Saudi Arabia.
Hans Henri P. Kluge, nominated by Belgium, has led WHO's Regional Office for Europe since 2020. Previously, he headed its Division of Health Systems and Public Health from 2009 to 2020. His earlier work included tuberculosis programs with WHO and Doctors Without Borders. He also helped establish WHO’s primary health care center in Almaty.
María P. Neira, Spain’s nominee, has led WHO’s work on environmental health and climate change. She previously served as Spain’s vice minister of health and headed its food safety agency. Neira began her humanitarian work with Doctors Without Borders in Central American refugee camps. Her medical background includes endocrinology and public health.
Budi Gunadi Sadikin, nominated by Indonesia, has served as health minister since December 2020. He led the country’s COVID-19 response and national vaccination program. Previously, he served as vice minister of state-owned enterprises and chief executive of Bank Mandiri. His career spans banking, industry and government.
Li Song, China’s nominee, has served as a secretary of the All-China Women’s Federation secretariat since September 2023. She previously headed the National Health Commission’s Department of Women and Children Health. Her work has focused on maternal and child health, alongside women’s rights and development. She holds a doctorate in medicine from Peking University’s School of Public Health.
Gevorg Tamamyan, nominated by Botswana, is an Armenian specialist in pediatric cancer and blood disorders. He heads the Pediatric Cancer and Blood Disorders Center of Armenia. He also leads Yerevan State Medical University’s Department of Pediatric Oncology and Hematology. Since 2024, he has served as president of the International Society of Pediatric Oncology’s Asian branch.
The candidates will meet member state representatives in Geneva on November 18-19. WHO will broadcast the forum in its six official languages.
In early 2027, the Executive Board will shortlist five candidates and interview them. It will then nominate up to three for consideration by the World Health Assembly.
A second candidates’ forum will take place on March 15, 2027.
The World Health Assembly will appoint the new director-general in May 2027. The successful candidate will take office on August 16, 2027.
Earlier, Qazinform News Agency reported that Kazakhstan welcomed the UAE’s nomination of Lana Zaki Nusseibeh for UN Secretary-General. She serves as the UAE’s Minister of State for Foreign Affairs.
